fact: The Iroquois Theatre was advertised as 'absolutely fireproof'
source: Timetable of Death: The Iroquois Theatre Fire of 1903, Nat Brandt (2003); also widely documented in contemporary newspaper accounts

fact: The fire occurred approximately 30 days after the theatre opened (opened November 23, 1903; fire on December 30, 1903)
source: Chicago Tribune historical archives; Wikipedia summary of Iroquois Theatre fire

fact: It was a Wednesday matinee with balconies packed with women and children
source: Timetable of Death, Nat Brandt (2003); contemporary accounts confirm a holiday matinee audience largely of women and children

fact: Exit doors were bolted or locked shut, and some lacked visible handles on the inside, reportedly to prevent non-paying patrons from entering
source: Chicago Historical Society records; 'Timetable of Death' by Nat Brandt; fire investigation testimony

fact: Some doors opened inward, causing bodies to pile up against exits
source: Widely documented in fire investigation reports and in 'Timetable of Death' by Nat Brandt. Note: some exits had European-style bascule locks unfamiliar to patrons rather than strictly opening inward — the script simplifies the mechanism.

fact: 602 people died in the Iroquois Theatre fire
source: Death toll figures vary between 572 and 602 depending on the source and whether delayed deaths are counted. The figure 602 appears in some accounts including Nat Brandt's book. The most commonly cited figure is approximately 602.
